name: VA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+17 district lean with incumbent Jennifer McClellan renominated
Overwhelming fundraising gap: McClellan $1.1M raised vs. Murray roughly $1,200
Prediction markets price McClellan at about 98% to win
No competitive polls or expert ratings; no outside spending on either side
model.rationale: McClellan combines a D+17 seat, incumbency, and a near-total fundraising advantage over Robert Murray, while markets price her at roughly 98% and no polling or ratings suggest competition. Every available signal points to a comfortable Democratic win in the mid-20s.
model.watch: Only an unforeseen scandal or a sudden wave of outside spending against McClellan could move this race, and nothing currently signals either.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Virginia's 4th District is a heavily Democratic seat, and incumbent Jennifer McClellan is seeking re-election after securing her party's nomination. Republican Robert Murray has raised roughly $1,200, leaving him with almost no resources, while McClellan has more than $1.1 million on hand. An independent candidate, Joan Bell, is also on the ballot but shows no measurable support.

Prediction markets give McClellan about a 98% chance of winning, and no public polls or expert ratings flag the race as competitive. The district's strong Democratic lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and the absence of outside spending on either side all point the same direction. Barring an unforeseen development, McClellan is positioned for a comfortable victory margin in the mid-20s.
